messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists
function.description: Retrieves a list of all artists whose works are present in a museum during a particular period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

period.description: The time period for which to retrieve the artists, e.g., 19th Century.

country.description: The country where the museum is located, optional parameter. Default: 'USA'

message.content:
**Famous 19th‑Century Dancers (Ballet & Other Forms)**  

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions / Roles |
|------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swiss/Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Renowned for her virtuosity and dramatic expressiveness; toured Europe and the U.S. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1888) | Italian | Influential choreographer and teacher; authored *L’Art de la Danse* (1845). |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of the Imperial Ballet; created *Swan Lake*, *The Sleeping Beauty*, *The Nutcracker*. |
| **Jean Coralli** (1799–1874) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle* (1841); known for his elegant style. |
| **Camille Saint‑Hilaire** (1810–1888) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle*; contributed to the development of Romantic ballet. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though her career peaked in the early 20th century, she was trained in the 19th‑century tradition and popularized the solo “dancer” form. |
| **John L. T. (John) T. (John) T.** | — | *[No record]* |
| **Eugène Scribe** (1791–1861) | French | Playwright and librettist; his works inspired many ballets of the era. |
| **Giovanni Battista Viotti** (1755–1824) | Italian | Composer whose music was used in 19th‑century ballets. |
| **Friedrich Schiller** (1759–1805) | German | Playwright; his dramas were adapted into ballets. |
| **Martha Graham** (1894–1991) | American | Though her career began in the 20th century, she was influenced by 19th‑century modern dance pioneers. |

*(Note: The table focuses on dancers and choreographers who shaped ballet in the 19th century. Other dance traditions—such as folk, opera, and early modern dance—had notable figures as well, but the most internationally recognized names come from the Romantic ballet movement.)*
